record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.context_brief: stability of complementability under small distortion
record.original_question: Does there exist ε1 > 0 such that whenever X is a complemented subspace of L1[0,1] and Y is a subspace of L1[0,1] with Banach-Mazur distance d(Y,X) < 1+ε for some ε ≤ ε1, the space Y must also be complemented? If so, how is the projection constant of Y controlled by the projection constant of X, possibly with ε1 depending on that projection constant?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. [B. Randrianantoanina] Does there exists an ε1 > 0 such that whenever X is a complemented subspace of L1 and Y is a subspace of L1 with d(Y,X) < 1 + ε with ε ≤ ε1 , then Y is complemented? If yes, how is the projection constant of Y related to that of X ? Maybe, ε1 depending on the projection constant K of X ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^1 = L^1[0,1]$ denote the classical Lebesgue space of (equivalence classes of) integrable functions on $[0,1]$. For closed subspaces $X, Y \subseteq L^1$, define the Banach-Mazur distance by
$$d(Y,X) = \inf\{\|T\|\cdot\|T^{-1}\| : T : Y \to X \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\}.$$
A closed subspace $Z \subseteq L^1$ is called complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection $P : L^1 \to L^1$ with range $Z$; the projection constant of $Z$ is $\lambda(Z) = \inf\{\|P\| : P \text{ is a bounded linear projection of } L^1 \text{ onto } Z\}$.

Decide the following:

(a) Does there exist a universal constant $\varepsilon_1 > 0$ such that whenever $X$ is a complemented subspace of $L^1$ and $Y$ is a closed subspace of $L^1$ with $d(Y,X) < 1+\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_1$, the subspace $Y$ must also be complemented in $L^1$?

(b) If the answer is affirmative, possibly with $\varepsilon_1 = \varepsilon_1(K)$ allowed to depend on the projection constant $K = \lambda(X)$, give a quantitative bound on the projection constant $\lambda(Y)$ in terms of $K$ and $\varepsilon$.
artifact.status_search_result: Randrianantoanina established that for isometric subspaces of $L^p$ (with $p$ outside an exceptional set), complementability transfers and the projection constant is preserved. However, no source located confirms a resolution of the almost-isometric ($d(Y,X)<1+\varepsilon$) stability question in $L^1$ with the quantitative control on the projection constant, and the broader complemented-subspace problem for $L^1$ remains open. Current status of this specific stability question could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: A note on Banach-Mazur problem (Randrianantoanina)
status_evidence.snippet: Randrianantoanina showed that if X and Y are isometric subspaces of Lp (p outside an exceptional set), and X is complemented in Lp then so is Y, with the same projection constant.
status_evidence.claim: The isometric version of the stability question has been addressed for Lp spaces, but the almost-isometric version in L1 is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the complemented subspace problem including L1 spaces; the structure of complemented subspaces of L1 remains a major open area.
status_evidence.claim: The complemented subspace problem for L1 is still an active open area.
